$comment: The scope object of spec §13j. Set by the field's experts, not by the agent and not by the owner. Versioned: a change here is a change to what the agent may work on.
principle: ageing is a progressive change in cell state that leaves a readable trace — a claim that has never been separately tested

set_by.$comment: roles, never names — naming a person in a design document commits them to something they have not agreed to. `named` is filled when a panel exists.

in.boundary: construction and evaluation, always net of composition
explicitly in scope, because the field's literature is a surviving tail

out.question: any recommendation to an individual
out.why: the adjacent commercial space sells exactly this

out.question: clinical practice
out.why: no clinical claim is available from a biomarker
out.goes_to: clinicians, given evidence the field does not have

out.question: the claim that a moved biomarker is a health outcome

adjacent.relation: shares methylation data, cohorts and confounders

claims_allowed: clock accuracy before AND after deconvolution
performance across institutional and seed-varied splits
outcome links when measured — and their absence when not
claims_forbidden: any claim about a named individual
any statement that a result is clinically actionable without the endpoint role's sign-off
would_move_the_boundary: rung 3 returning null — if clocks do not predict outcomes net of age and composition, the scope is wrong at its centre and the response is contraction or closure, not a better clock
$watch_comment: if this rung stays blocked by a dependency the scope put out of bounds, the boundary is in the wrong place (§13j)
